newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - Telefonos de Mexico higher.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - Telefonos de Mexico higher.

text.p: Telefonos de Mexico was trading higher in an otherwise quiet session for Latin American American Depositary Receipts (ADRs), dealers said Wednesday.
"Its pretty quiet," said one trader, referring to trading in U.S.-registered stocks from the region. "Not much stuff is going on."
Telefonos, Mexico's telephone company known as Telmex, was 1-3/8 higher at 46-7/8 on a volume of two million shares following a first call by Morgan Stanley on Mexico's new economic development plan.
The report welcomed the plan, but said the government would have to recapitalize the banking system in order to make it work, among other measures.
Brazil's telephone holding company Telebras SA was 1/8 higher at 134-5/8 after it released higher than expected earnings, a consolidated net profit of 965 million reais for the January-April period.

Canadian stock Newbridge Networks Corp was also trading higher on its results, up 5/8 at 40-5/8. The integrated digital network maker reported a net loss after charges of C$0.17 a share for the fourth quarter ending April 30.
Excluding the charges, the company said its net profit was C$0.38 a share, in line with results for the same period last year. "People seem happy with the results," one dealer said.
Canada's Arakis Energy Corp was also active, up 9/64 at 4-1/4. Dutch ADR Philips Electronics NV was trading 2-3/4 up at 60-1/2, while South Korea's SK Telecom Co was down 1/4 at 10.
Decliners led advancers 234 to 227 among 814 ADRs. The ADR group was up 0.13 percent on a total volume of 39.2 million ADRs.
ADRs allow U.S trade of foreign shares.
